title: Supetar with Teens: Family Travel Guide 2027
metaDescription: Supetar with teenagers: beaches, aquapark, kayaking, quad tours, Vidova Gora, ferry prices from Split and tips for a family stay on Brač in 2027.
content:
## Is Supetar Good for Teenagers?

Yes, with realistic expectations. Supetar is the largest town on Brač and the island's main ferry port. It is calm, safe and walkable. It is not a nightlife town. Teens who like swimming, jumping off piers, kayaking, cycling and day trips will be busy. Older teens who want clubs and large crowds may find the evenings quiet. Bol and Hvar are the usual escapes.

## Getting to Supetar from Split

The Jadrolinija car ferry (line 631) is the standard route. It crosses in about 50 minutes and runs up to 14 or more times a day in high season. Departures start around 05:00 and the last ones leave close to midnight.

- Adult foot passenger: €6.50 in high season, about €4.40 off-season
- Child (3 to 12 years): about €3.20 in high season
- Standard car (under 5 m): about €26.10 in high season, from about €18 off-season
- Bicycle: about €6.20 in high season

A fast passenger catamaran (Krilo) also crosses in about 20 minutes, but it costs considerably more than the car ferry and does not take cars. Car ferries to Supetar rarely cancel in bad weather. Catamarans cancel more often on strong jugo (south wind) days.

## Best Activities for Teens in Supetar

### Beaches with Things to Do

Banj Beach is the most developed beach in town. It has sunbeds, beach bars, a volleyball court, pedal boats, kayak and SUP rental, and the Wibit aquapark with floating obstacles and slides. Right beside it, Tri Mosta is known for three large piers where teens spend summer afternoons jumping into the sea. Both are a short walk west of the harbour along the promenade. The seabed is gravel and pebbles, so water shoes help.

### Kayaking and Water Sports

Kayak hire in Supetar Bay costs about €20 per hour for a single kayak. Guided kayak tours run from Supetar along the coast through Splitska to Postira. Several local operators also offer boat excursions to Hvar, Vis (Blue Cave) and the Blue Lagoon near Drvenik.

### Cycling

The coastal road west to Splitska and Postira and the road east towards Sutivan and Milna both work for teens who ride regularly. Bike and e-bike rental shops operate along the waterfront in season. Ride early in July and August, because the midday heat on exposed roads is strong.

### Quad Safari and Horse Riding

Quad tours through olive groves and inland villages cost about €120 per person for 2 to 3 hours. Confirm minimum age and licence rules with the operator before booking.

### Culture That Does Not Bore Teenagers

The church bell tower in the harbour area can be climbed for a view over the town. Supetar cemetery, on the peninsula west of the centre, holds work by the sculptor Ivan Rendić. Both are short stops of 20 to 30 minutes. Škrip, the oldest settlement on Brač, and its olive oil museum need a car or bike.

## Day Trips from Supetar with Teens

### Zlatni Rat and Bol

Zlatni Rat is the most famous beach in Croatia. It is also the main windsurfing spot on Brač. Buses run from Supetar to Bol in under an hour, and the journey is cheap, about €7 per person. Check the last return bus from Bol (traditionally around 21:00) because it fills up fast.

The taxi alternative costs about €60 to €75 each way and takes around 40 minutes. For a family of four it is still reasonable. For a solo teen it is not.

### Vidova Gora and Blaca Monastery

Vidova Gora rises to about 780 m, the highest point in the Adriatic islands. It has views across Hvar, Šolta and the mainland. Blaca Monastery needs a drive plus about a 40-minute hike. Start before 10:00 in summer.

### Island Boat Trips

Full-day boat trips to Hvar, the Blue Cave on Biševo and the Blue Lagoon include swimming stops. Prices vary by operator and season. Book a day ahead in July and August.

## Where to Eat with Teens

The harbour front has many pizzerias and grill restaurants, which work for picky eaters. The largest supermarkets are in the south of town, beside the main road. Konoba Kala, which is listed in the Michelin Guide, suits one special family dinner.

## Local Tips for Families

- Rent a car for at least two days if the family has more than three people. Bus times limit spontaneous plans, and taxis add up.
- Take the ferry at off-peak hours in July and August. Early morning and late evening queues are shorter.
- Pack water shoes. The pebbles at Banj and Tri Mosta hurt bare feet.
- Arrive at the beach before 10:00 for shade and sunbeds in peak season.
- Taking the taxi to Bol for a day at Zlatni Rat sounds easy, but at €120 or more return it costs far more than the bus for little extra comfort. Use the bus and keep the taxi for the late return.

## Best Time to Visit

June and September give warm sea and fewer crowds. July and August have the most activities running, but also the highest prices and the busiest ferries. Many beach facilities, including water sports, run from late spring to early autumn.

faq.question: Is Supetar good for teenagers?
faq.answer: Yes, for teens who enjoy swimming, kayaking, cycling and day trips. Banj Beach has an aquapark and Tri Mosta has jumping piers. Evenings are quiet, so older teens who want nightlife may prefer Bol or a Hvar day trip.

faq.question: How much is the ferry from Split to Supetar?
faq.answer: A Jadrolinija car ferry ticket costs €6.50 per adult and about €3.20 per child in high season. A standard car costs about €26.10. The crossing takes around 50 minutes.

faq.question: How do you get from Supetar to Zlatni Rat?
faq.answer: Take the bus from Supetar to Bol, which takes under an hour and costs about €7, then walk to the beach. A taxi costs about €60 to €75 each way. Check the last bus back in the evening.

faq.question: What can teens do in Supetar on a rainy day?
faq.answer: Options are limited. The bell tower, the cemetery with Rendić sculptures and the Škrip olive oil museum are the main choices. A ferry trip to Split for the Diocletian's Palace area and shops is the most popular wet-weather option.

faq.question: Can teenagers go to Bol or Split by themselves?
faq.answer: Many families allow it, since Croatia is generally safe and local teens use buses and ferries in summer. Check bus and ferry times in advance and make sure the teen knows the last return departure.

quickAnswer: Supetar suits families with teens aged 12 to 17 who like water activities. Banj Beach has a Wibit aquapark, Tri Mosta has jumping piers, and kayaking, cycling and quad tours start nearby. Split is a 50-minute ferry away (€6.50 adult). Older teens may find evenings quiet.
